content.title: SeeMe in Prague!
content.summary: Our team had the opportunity to represent CIME at the 29th SESAM conference in Prague, held from June 19th to 21st.

content.text: Our team had the opportunity to represent CIME at the 29th SESAM conference in Prague, held from June 19th to 21st. SESAM, the Society for Simulation in Europe, is dedicated to advancing healthcare simulation, and this year's conference brought together experts from around the world to exchange knowledge and best practices.

Dr. Faisal Ismail, Regional Director of CIME South Asia, was a key speaker at the conference. He presented his research on the challenges and opportunities of using simulation in healthcare education in developing countries. He highlighted how simulation helps educators create safe learning environments, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) where access to such tools is limited. He also discussed ways to improve accessibility in these regions, stressing the need for global collaboration.

Dr. Selina Hasan, an Education Advisor from CIME Karachi, presented two abstracts for oral communication at SESAM 2024. The first abstract, titled "Brain Attack Team: A High-Fidelity Interprofessional Stroke Code Training in an LMIC," and second, "Saving Tiny Lives: Assessing the Effectiveness of High-Fidelity Simulation for Training on Neonatal Resuscitation in an LMIC".

Furthermore, Dr. Michael Moneypenny, Regional Director of CIME East Africa, also attended the conference, which was a great opportunity to share ideas and connect with others dedicated to advancing healthcare education through simulation. We look forward to participating in the next SESAM conference in 2025.
